findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the snippet window may span concatenated-field boundaries or must clamp to the boundaries of the single field containing the match, resolving the concatenated-slice vs 'comes from that field' wording.
evidence: 'the reducer builds a case-preserving searchable string in the exact existing field order ... then slices the case-preserving string'
'If the match occurs only in a tag, identifier, or comment, the snippet comes from that field; this bounded window is permitted but the full field/comment body is never returned.'
findings.finding: The snippet spec mixes two mechanisms that can conflict at field boundaries: it says the window is sliced from the case-preserving CONCATENATED string (title+description+tags+id+alias+jira+comments), yet also says 'If the match occurs only in a tag, identifier, or comment, the snippet comes from that field.' A slice of the concatenated string centered on a match near a field boundary could bleed the tail of one field into the head of the next, contradicting the field-scoped promise.
scenarios: A positive term matches at the very end of the title field; a 240-char window centered on it pulls in the beginning of the description, so the snippet spans two fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify that the window is clamped to the byte/char range of the field that owns the matched occurrence (never crossing into an adjacent field), then centered and ellipsized within that clamped range.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how snippet indexing stays aligned between the case-preserving and lowercased copies (e.g. use casefold/lower per-position with a length-preserving guarantee, or locate via a case-insensitive search that returns an index into the ORIGINAL string, or fall back gracefully when lengths diverge).
evidence: Plan: 'It locates the first occurrence of the first matching positive free-text term ... case-insensitively, then slices the case-preserving string.'

reducer/_query.py lowercases text terms via tok.lower(); reducer/search.py _haystack lowercases the whole haystack, so matching is done on lowercased text while the plan slices the case-preserving copy.
Python str.lower() can change length for some code points (e.g. U+0130), breaking a positional index computed on the lowercased copy when applied to the original.
findings.finding: The snippet mechanism assumes the lowercased comparison copy is index-aligned with the case-preserving copy, but str.lower() is not length-preserving for all Unicode (e.g. certain dotted/ligature characters expand), so slicing the case-preserving string at an index found in the lowercased copy can desynchronize and produce a shifted or garbled snippet window.
findings.location: Output contract — snippet paragraph ('a case-preserving searchable string ... and a lowercased comparison copy ... then slices the case-preserving string')
scenarios: A ticket description containing a code point whose lowercase form has a different length, before the matched term, shifts every subsequent index and the snippet window lands off-position.
Non-ASCII ticket content (international tickets) triggers subtly wrong snippet boundaries.
findings.suggested_fix: Locate the match with a case-insensitive scan that returns an index into the case-preserving string directly (e.g. compare original[i:i+len(term)].lower() == term over i) rather than searching a separately-lowercased copy, eliminating the index-alignment assumption.
